intent_en: To demonstrate that decarbonizing the electricity, residential, commercial, and transportation sectors is the key to solving the majority of US carbon emission problems.
previous_intent: To illustrate the breakdown of US carbon dioxide emissions by economic sector and highlight that decarbonizing electricity, residential, commercial, and transportation sectors would address a significant portion of the problem.
narration_support: If electricity, residential, commercial, and transportation were mostly decarbonized, you'd have solved a lot of the problem.
chart_support: Pie chart displaying the breakdown of US carbon dioxide emissions by economic sector.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly argues that targeting specific sectors (electricity, residential, commercial, transportation) solves the problem, while the chart visualizes the emission distribution across these sectors plus industrial, showing they comprise the bulk of emissions.
